In Kaczynski's Technological Slavery, he mentions the Earth First! movement to illustrate how ecological movements are prone to being overtaken by Leftists:

>Whenever a movement of resistance begins to emerge, these leftists (or whatever you choose to call them) come swarming to it like flies to honey until they outnumber the original members of the movement, take it over, and turn it into just another leftist faction, thereby emasculating it. The history of "Earth First!" provides an elegant example of this process.

>As it was originally constituted in the early 1980s, Earth First! may have had the makings of a genuine revolutionary movement. But it indiscriminately invited all comers, and-of course!-the majority of comers were leftish types. These swamped the movement numerically and then took it over, changing its character.

Does anyone have any more examples of this phenomenon? I can think of few similar ones:

>The Sierra Club 
this movement was all about opposing mass immigration due to it being a huge environmental concern, but then some David Gelbaum gave them a $200 million bribe to start shilling for immigration, and now their cornerstone efforts are completely diluted

>Extinction Rebellion 
one of the founders flat-out admitted this movement isn't about saving the environment, but rather dismantling "patriarchy", "European civilization", "heteronormativity", "class hierarchy", etc.

>Greta Thunberg 
her mask slipped (or rather, the mask of her "owners") when she recently accused patriarchy, racism and colonialism of creating the climate crisis

Anyone got more? I know Leftism creeps up on other types of movements too (see: Atheism+), but I'm primarily interested in environmental ones.
